title: Averaged Mirror Descent and Dual Gradient Methods: Convergent Algorithms for Entropic Gromov-Wasserstein Problems
abstract: arXiv:2609.31848v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance measures the discrepancy between metric measure (mm) spaces and identifies optimal alignments between them based solely on their intrinsic structure. Since it identifies isomorphic mm spaces, it provides a natural notion of distance for heterogeneous datasets which may admit isomorphic representations. In order to accelerate computation of GW distances, many practitioners employ entropic regularization to obtain an Entropic GW (EGW) problem. The most popular EGW solver is the Mirror Descent (MD) algorithm, which reduces EGW computations to an iterative process where an entropic optimal transport (EOT) problem is solved at each iteration. Despite its widespread use, the convergence of MD for this problem has only been established for restricted classes of costs. translated_abstract: Gromov-Wasserstein（GW）距离度量了度量测度（mm）空间之间的差异，并仅基于其内在结构来识别它们之间的最优对齐。由于该距离能够识别同构的度量测度空间，它为可能存在同构表示的异构数据集提供了一种自然的距离概念。为了加速GW距离的计算，许多研究者采用熵正则化方法，从而得到熵GW（EGW）问题。最流行的EGW求解器是镜像下降（MD）算法，它将EGW的计算转化为一个迭代过程，其中每次迭代需要求解一个熵最优传输（EOT）问题。尽管MD被广泛使用，但针对该问题的MD收敛性目前仅在受限的代价函数类别中得到证明。另一方面，最近提出的对偶梯度方法适用于一般的代价函数，但需要选择一个依赖于（原文在此处截断）的步长
tldr: 该论文提出了平均化的镜像下降方法与对偶梯度方法，为一般代价函数下的熵Gromov-Wasserstein问题首次建立了具有严格收敛保证的算法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes averaged mirror descent and dual gradient methods, establishing convergent algorithms with guarantees for entropic Gromov-Wasserstein problems under general cost functions.
